target_backend_amendment: Before fitting or hardware submission, use threaded Quimb target generation. The original Aer wheel embeds single-threaded OpenBLAS. Retain the completed Aer bond-128 target, Quimb CPU benchmark and their finite-bond numerical disagreement. Target acceptance still requires the declared same-engine bond convergence and feasibility stability checks.
scope: One exploratory, previously studied FLP instance with six facilities and six customers (42 qubits). Complete 12-step annealing only; no substitution of a half schedule. Direct MPS target generation, AQC-Tensor MPS fitting and MPS event contractions. No dense state vector at this width. Classical target convergence is a numerical check, not an exact certificate.
selection: At each depth retain the numerically verified fit with greatest target overlap. Hardware screening selects the native circuit with highest measured feasible probability, with ties resolved by target overlap and then smaller CZ depth. Freeze selection before independent confirmation. No minimum approximation fidelity for hardware eligibility. Target and fit numerical checks remain mandatory.
inference: Only independent confirmation shots estimate effects. Compare selected native preparation against complete annealing, fitted product preparation and fixed shallow AQC. Feasibility is primary; optimum probability secondary. All six two-sided block-stratified conditional comparisons share one Holm family. Report pointwise block MOVER intervals and conservative CP sensitivity intervals. All candidates, failures, selection shots and counts retained. A single instance does not establish asymptotic scaling.
execution: Randomize circuit order in two blocks per phase. Raw counts with no feasibility repair, postselection, twirling or dynamical decoupling. Preserve live processor family/revision, calibration and circuit hashes. Persist intent and job receipt; never automatically repeat ambiguous or failed submissions.
